articles.title: EBA reviews how banks report sustainable activities
articles.summary: A July consultation examined simpler and more useful sustainability disclosures.
paragraphs: The European Banking Authority opened a discussion on selected indicators used in Taxonomy disclosures on 1 July. Its stated aim was to simplify reporting and make the information more useful. The consultation closed on 12 August 2026.

The paper covered indicators for banks and investment firms, including fee income, trading activities and group reporting. It was a consultation step towards technical advice, rather than a new sustainability label for retail accounts.

For an account customer, a bank's environmental reporting and the terms of a particular product answer different questions. A sustainability claim does not explain whether a card carries an annual charge or which transactions are included.

Our view: readers should be able to inspect both. Look for a clearly defined environmental claim and its supporting disclosure, then assess the account's ordinary costs independently. This July announcement alone cannot establish whether any named account meets a customer's environmental preferences.

articles.title: 36 providers selected for the digital euro pilot
articles.summary: The selection advances testing, rather than a public launch.
paragraphs: The ECB announced the selection of 36 payment service providers for its digital euro pilot on 14 July 2026. More than 50 providers had applied. The selected group includes banks and non-bank providers across the euro area.

The planned exercise will run for 12 months from the second half of 2027. It will test technical functions, operating processes and user experience in a controlled environment involving central bank staff and selected merchants.

The beta digital euro used in the pilot will not have legal-tender status. Selection therefore does not mean that customers can already open a public digital euro account with a participating provider.

For people comparing current accounts, the useful distinction is between a future payment project and a service available today. Our view is to evaluate a bank on the tariff, payment functions and support it currently offers, while following the pilot for evidence of future capabilities.

articles.title: July survey shows banks tightening lending standards
articles.summary: Banks reported tighter criteria, with differences across borrowers.
paragraphs: Euro area banks reported tighter credit standards in the ECB's July 2026 bank lending survey. The net share reporting tightening was 7% for business lending, 9% for housing loans and 12% for consumer credit in the second quarter.

Risk perceptions and reduced willingness to take risk were important drivers. Demand for business loans rose slightly, while demand from households weakened. These are survey measures of changes, not the percentage of all applications rejected.
A current account and a credit decision should not be treated as the same product choice. Opening an account does not establish that a customer will qualify for an overdraft or a future loan.

Our view: assess the payment account on its own terms first. If credit is important, obtain a separate eligibility assessment and written offer. A sector-wide survey helps explain the environment, but cannot predict a particular bank's decision on an individual application.

articles.title: Cards account for most euro area non-cash payments
articles.summary: July's release describes payment behaviour in the second half of 2025.
paragraphs: Statistics released by the ECB on 22 July show that cards represented 57% of the number of non-cash payments in the euro area in the second half of 2025. Credit transfers accounted for 21% and direct debits for 14%.
Contactless card payments increased by 11.9% compared with the same period a year earlier. The figures describe a past reporting period; they are not a July 2026 count of transactions.

For an account comparison, the practical point is that the card deserves its own line. An account can have no monthly maintenance charge while a particular physical card, replacement or delivery still costs money.

Our view: start with the card you actually need. Compare virtual and physical access, recurring charges and the operations you use. Aggregate payment popularity does not make every paid card worthwhile, and it does not remove the need to check the provider's tariff.

articles.title: Financial supervisors focus on cyber risks from frontier AI
articles.summary: The authorities called for stronger governance and operational resilience.
paragraphs: The EU's three financial supervisory authorities issued a joint statement on 31 July about ICT risks associated with frontier AI models. It calls for a consistent, risk-based supervisory approach across financial sectors.

The statement emphasises governance, risk management, prevention, detection and response. It also discusses oversight of critical technology providers under DORA. It does not announce a ban on AI use in banking.

For customers, the presence of an AI feature in a banking app says little on its own about reliability or accountability. Convenient automation and access to a clear support route need to be assessed separately.

Our view: when choosing a digital account, consider how you would freeze a card, recover access and contact the provider if an automated process went wrong. Those are practical service questions. This supervisory statement is an industry risk signal, rather than a security rating of any individual bank or app.

articles.title: Reading July's monetary data without confusing it with bank offers
articles.sourceName: ECB monetary developments for July, 27 August 2026
articles.summary: Economy-wide money statistics and individual deposit terms serve different purposes.
paragraphs: The ECB published its monetary developments release for July 2026 on 27 August. This statistical series follows money and lending developments across the euro area, rather than advertising the terms of an individual bank account.

Its publication date and reference month are different. That distinction matters when reading financial headlines: an August announcement can describe July activity, and later statistical releases may revise the picture.
A saver cannot read an available account interest rate directly from a monetary aggregate. Choosing a product still requires the provider's own rate, conditions, balance limits and applicable period.

Our view: use central bank statistics to understand the wider environment, then return to the product document for an actual comparison. Record the date of both sources. An account's advertised rate, a central bank policy rate and the growth rate of money describe different things and should not be presented as interchangeable.

articles.title: Digital euro pilot opens its call to online merchants
articles.summary: Merchants were invited to help test a controlled payment environment.
paragraphs: The Eurosystem opened a call on 15 September for euro area e-commerce and mobile-commerce merchants to join the digital euro pilot. It follows the earlier selection of payment service providers.

The announcement sets an application deadline of 27 October 2026 at 17:00 CET. The planned 12-month pilot begins in the second half of 2027 and uses a beta payment environment to examine functionality and user experience.
A merchant call is a preparation milestone. It does not mean that digital euro acceptance is already a standard feature available through every business bank account.

Our view: businesses comparing accounts today should distinguish existing acceptance services from announced experiments. Current charges, settlement arrangements and support remain the immediate comparison points. Pilot feedback may inform a future product, but it is not a substitute for a provider's live service description. Readers considering participation should consult the official call for its complete eligibility and application requirements.

articles.title: EBA updates its approach to banks' outside service providers
articles.sourceName: EBA third-party risk guidelines announcement, 18 September 2026
articles.summary: The framework focuses on arrangements supporting critical or important functions.
paragraphs: The EBA published final guidelines on third-party risk management on 18 September. The announcement concentrates on arrangements supporting critical or important functions, where disruption could materially impair a financial entity.

The guidelines address the relationship from assessment and contracting through monitoring and exit planning, across ICT and non-ICT services. The EBA describes a two-year transitional period and alignment with the broader DORA framework.
Customers usually see a bank's brand and app, rather than its supplier network. A polished interface therefore cannot answer every question about how the service would respond to a disruption.

Our view: compare usable support and recovery routes alongside fees. Ask where service notices appear and how to reach the provider if the normal app is unavailable. These guidelines concern institutions' risk management; they are not evidence that a particular bank has suffered an outage or that a named supplier is unsafe.

articles.title: Consumers' inflation expectations rose in August
articles.summary: The survey measures household expectations, rather than realised inflation.
paragraphs: The ECB's August Consumer Expectations Survey, released on 18 September, showed median expected inflation over the next year rising to 3.0%, from 2.9% in July. Perceived inflation over the previous year stayed at 3.5%.

Expected nominal income growth was unchanged at 1.0%, while expected spending growth remained 3.6%. These results describe what surveyed consumers expected, not an official forecast or the eventual inflation outcome.
For household banking decisions, the difference between nominal interest and purchasing power deserves attention. A headline savings rate alone cannot explain how a balance's real value will change.

Our view: keep everyday account costs and savings returns visible as separate figures. A welcome benefit is also different from a recurring return. Use the survey as context for financial uncertainty, while checking each product's actual rate, term and restrictions rather than treating an expectation as a guaranteed result.

articles.title: Nearly ten million people joined the euro banknote design survey
articles.summary: A future redesign does not require customers to exchange their cash today.
paragraphs: The ECB reported on 23 September that 9.96 million people had taken part in its survey on future euro banknote designs. The survey ran from 23 July to 21 September 2026.

Responses will inform the design process alongside other assessments. The announcement envisages the new series entering circulation gradually in the early 2030s and states that existing banknotes will remain valid alongside it.
For account customers, banknote design and access to cash are separate issues. An account's ATM conditions, branch services and card format determine how practical cash access is today.

Our view: a story about a future series is not a reason to pay someone to replace existing notes. When comparing a digital account, consider the cash withdrawals you need and the charges or access restrictions that may apply. The survey milestone concerns future design choices, rather than an immediate change to a bank's cash services.

articles.title: ECB explores an instant-payment connection with Brazil
articles.summary: The proposal is being assessed; a consumer service has not been launched.
paragraphs: The ECB announced approval to assess a possible connection between the Eurosystem's TIPS platform and Brazil's Pix system on 24 September. The work with Brazil's central bank covers technical, operational, legal and business questions.

The stated ambition is to facilitate faster and potentially cheaper cross-border payments. A feasibility assessment, however, is not the same as a completed connection or a retail service available in a banking app.
For someone sending money abroad, speed is only one part of the comparison. Currency conversion, the amount received and any intermediary charges can also affect the result.

Our view: compare services that are actually available for the relevant destination and currency. Ask for the total amount debited and the expected amount received. An infrastructure announcement is useful evidence of direction, but cannot establish the final exchange rate, customer fee or launch date of a future transfer product.

articles.title: European banks report strong buffers in the latest risk dashboard
articles.sourceName: EBA Q2 risk dashboard announcement, 25 September 2026
articles.summary: Sector-wide strength still leaves differences between individual institutions.
paragraphs: The EBA's second-quarter risk dashboard, released on 25 September, described EU/EEA banks as having robust capital and liquidity. It reported a Common Equity Tier 1 ratio of 16.1% and a liquidity coverage ratio of 158.5%.

The non-performing loan ratio stood at 1.8%. The authority also highlighted geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainty, and differences between countries and portfolios. The dashboard describes the sector rather than giving every bank an identical assessment.
That distinction matters when choosing an account. A positive aggregate result is useful background, but it does not identify the legal entity behind a product or explain its contractual protections.

Our view: keep institutional identity, account conditions and customer service in the comparison. A general sector dashboard cannot tell you whether an app fits your needs, what an overseas withdrawal costs or how an individual complaint would be handled. Strong averages should inform context, rather than replace product research.

articles.title: Digital euro innovation work opens to a broader group
articles.summary: Experimentation and exploration will examine possible future services.
paragraphs: The Eurosystem announced a new call for digital euro innovation activities on 28 September. Participants can include payment providers, technology businesses, merchants, consumer associations, public bodies and researchers.

The two workstreams cover practical experimentation and exploration of technologies for possible future releases. The ECB says an issuance decision would follow the adoption of the relevant EU legislation; preparation does not itself settle that decision.

This wider involvement matters because a payment method needs to work for people accepting money as well as those sending it. Useful design must address ordinary transactions, rather than technical demonstrations alone.

Our view: judge innovation announcements by the problem they aim to solve and the evidence that follows. Potential features should remain clearly labelled as potential. They should not be mixed into a current-account comparison as if every customer could already use them or as proof that a particular account is better.

articles.title: EBA sets out its banking priorities for 2027
articles.summary: Payments, resilience and supervisory efficiency appear in the forward work plan.
paragraphs: The EBA published its 2027 Work Programme on 30 September 2026. It groups its priorities around efficiency, resilience and transformation, with work on banking rules, payments and digital finance.

The announced agenda includes preparation for the new payment services framework, crisis-management and deposit-insurance reforms, supervisory convergence, and continuing activity under DORA and MiCA. A work programme describes planned activity; it does not make every item an immediately applicable customer rule.
For a retail customer, dates and legal status are essential. A consultation, a final technical standard and a rule that already applies to an account are different stages.

Our view: coverage of banking regulation should state which stage has been reached and avoid promising benefits before they exist. Account comparisons still need the provider's current documents. The programme helps readers follow the direction of supervision without replacing the terms that govern an account today.

articles.title: USDC becomes the EU's first significant e-money token
articles.summary: The classification changes supervisory responsibilities under MiCA.
paragraphs: The EBA announced on 14 October that USDC, issued by Circle Internet Financial Europe SAS, had been classified as a significant e-money token under MiCA. It is the first token to receive that classification in the EU.

The announcement schedules dual supervision from 12 November 2026. Certain responsibilities, including areas concerning reserves, liquidity and redemption planning, move to the EBA, while other areas remain with France's ACPR.

A significant-token classification describes regulatory treatment. It should not be presented as a recommendation to buy the token or as evidence that it is interchangeable with a euro current account.

Our view: customers should identify exactly what they hold, who owes them money and which terms apply before comparing digital-finance products. A banking app can contain different kinds of products. A supervisory milestone is a reason to read the details, rather than a shortcut around understanding the product and its risks.
